messages:
Ruth (Finance): Heads-up: AP put vendor invoice VN-2026-744 on hold. Bot says 'price variance' and 'no PO amendment'. Can AP confirm what's missing? :clipboard:

Ollie (AP): ap-bot: HOLD_REASON=PRICE_VARIANCE; invoice unit price $0.092/hr vs PO 7202 at $0.072/hr. No amendment or PO update referenced. Need either a reissued invoice under PO 7202 or an executed amendment that sets the new price and effective date.

Dina (Vendor Ops): Vendor claims they updated pricing in their billing portal on 2026-03-05 and invoices are auto-generated. They attached a portal screenshot and an unsigned email from their rep saying "pricing updated per renewal conversation." No DocuSign.

Ruth (Finance): We can't accept portal changes or unsigned sales notes as a contract amendment. For audit we need a signed amendment or reissue under the existing PO. If vendor insists on the new rate, ask them to provide an executed change order referencing SOW #CL-2025 and effective date.

procurement-bot: Note: procurement policy requires written, signed amendments for any unit price changes >5%. Current change = 27.8%.

Ollie (AP): To expedite, if vendor reissues invoice at the PO rate we'll pay the undisputed portion immediately. For any additional amount we need Procurement + Finance approval with a signed amendment.

Dina (Vendor Ops): Reached out to vendor asking them to either (A) reissue VN-2026-744 under PO 7202 at $0.072/hr or (B) send an executed amendment via DocuSign by EOD. I also asked them to pause collections.

Vendor Billing (via Dina): "We can reissue under the current PO for this cycle. We'll send a formal amendment for future invoices. DocuSign link will be sent to your procurement contact."

Ollie (AP): New invoice VN-2026-744v2 uploaded and matched to PO 7202. Verified amounts and routing for payment. Closing hold. Ticket AP-8465. :white_check_mark:

Ruth (Finance): Thanks everyone. Dina please confirm when we receive the DocuSign amendment so Procurement can review and update vendor master.

Dina (Vendor Ops): Will do. Also asking vendor to include clause language clarifying effective date won't be retroactive unless explicitly signed.
